text:
Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P3 feature work. Current ViewerModel owns an immutable Vector[SliceLayer]; ViewerReducer.reduce returns ViewerSession, not a new model. Simply adding ReorderLayers/SetColorizer to that action enum cannot change model-owned layers under the existing return contract. Use a validated model-update API and explicit host adoption, or deliberately revise the model/session ownership contract; do not hide mutable model replacement behind the pure reducer.

Current cache fact: SliceSampleKey includes the entire SliceLayer plus geometry/timepoint; SliceRasterKey adds window/threshold. Reordering the same layer values does not itself introduce an order component into either key. The missing host/model update path and cache retention must be assessed separately from cache-key design. Colorizer is part of the typed layer and TypedSample captures it, so replacement cannot blindly reuse a previously colorized or colorizer-bound sample. These are source observations, not runtime hit-rate measurements.

Refined acceptance:
- Validate duplicate/unknown IDs and define complete-permutation versus partial-order semantics explicitly; never silently drop unmentioned layers or invalidate the nonempty/unique-layer model invariants.
- Keep replacement colorizers consistent with the layer value type; do not cast an arbitrary existential Colorizer into a scalar/label layer. Preserve source, geometry, timepoint and sampling identity deliberately.
- Show the host can adopt the new model while preserving relevant session state and caches for unchanged layer values. Determine whether raw sample/colorizer separation is needed before promising sample reuse on recoloring.
- On JVM/JS, verify changed compositing order and changed colormap pixels, unchanged-layer cache hits, invalid update refusal and absence of stale colors. An aggregate cache-hit count alone is not proof of correct colorizer replacement.
- Neuropublish controller-rebuild observations are historical consumer context; do not claim that external application now adopts any new API. No implementation or new tests were performed in this assessment.
